trajectory_summary: The call opens cooperatively but reveals almost immediately that the customer already has a 15+ year old SolarCity system and has already been quoted by Ion for a battery/backup solution, making this an orphaned-flow scenario the rep never formally runs. The rep escalates via hold to resolve an unfamiliar sizing question and returns with a disqualification (system too large for a battery), which the customer accepts calmly.
outcome_dispute: The v1 outcome tag is unknown; observed outcome should be recorded as dq. The call ends with the rep stating the specialist determined the system is disqualified for backup/battery, and no appointment, callback time, or next step is offered.

observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep explicitly relays that a specialist disqualified the customer's request because the existing system size is incompatible with a battery/backup add-on. No appointment, callback time, or next step is set — the call ends with pleasantries and no owned next action.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: This call never reached a bill_amount question because the customer already has solar and the conversation redirected to a battery/backup inquiry; no utility bill figure was ever discussed. The closest analog — the 10kW system size — was captured but not flipped into a reason to act.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never directly asked what interested him in solar/backup — the reason emerged organically when the rep asked if he was looking for a backup generator. The customer clearly stated the outage-driven pain point, but the rep never referenced it again, including at the DQ moment where acknowledging the unresolved outage problem would have closed the call more gracefully.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: I was trying to get a specialist to come talk to you, but I was really fighting for you. But they they said your your kilowatt size is too big, and it's too big for a battery or a backup.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep never ran the standard orphaned_flow question sequence (ownership status, system working/not, clean panel-size capture) before going on a ~1-minute hold mid-call. This scenario — existing solar customer wanting backup only — is exactly what orphaned_flow exists to structure, and running it up front would have surfaced the sizing issue faster or given the specialist better info, without leaving the customer waiting on hold for an answer that came back as a flat no.

The rep never reflects it back or treats it as a flag to check before promising a specialist; it's filed silently and only resurfaces as bad news after a hold.

key_moments.stewart_read: This is the customer's core pain point — frequent outages in a rural area with unreliable lines — functionally equivalent to a bill-pain anchor for this backup-focused lead. The rep never acknowledges the inconvenience or hardship before pivoting to procedural questions about contracts and prior quotes.

The rep's follow-up ("did you like that quote or not really?") gets a partial answer ("It was on the high side") but the rep never asks who quoted it, when, or what was included — competitive/internal intel that would help avoid redundant outreach or correctly price-anchor a callback.
